key_insight: Potential-energy landscapes and statistical sampling provide a unified framework linking established materials theory with modern AI-driven discovery.
engineering_relevance: This practitioner-oriented guide helps engineers connect atomistic simulations, property prediction, and data-driven workflows for materials discovery and design.
method: Connect force fields, density-functional theory, and many-body methods through shared physical concepts.
Explain statistical sampling, property prediction, high-throughput workflows, and materials databases.
Examine atomistic representations, graph neural networks, and generative models through symmetry and probabilistic foundations.
evidence_signal: The abstract describes a pedagogical monograph informed by the author's research experience, without reporting datasets, quantitative benchmarks, or comparative evaluations.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish the accuracy, efficiency, or reliability of any specific AI-driven discovery workflow.
paper_title: A Practitioner's Guide to Materials Theory and Computation in the Age of Big Data and Artificial Intelligence
